title: Finite-energy two-way assisted capacities: Exact formulas for multimode loss and fading
abstract: We study quantum communication, entanglement distribution, and secret-key generation through multimode bosonic loss and fading channels, assisted by local quantum operations and two-way classical communication. Using sector teleportation, we determine the exact two-way quantum and secret-key capacities of multimode pure-loss channels under a mean photon-number constraint, allowing arbitrary adaptive quantum protocols. We extend these results to continuous frequency-dependent loss under a power constraint and identify the optimal allocation of photons among optical modes. For constant loss over an unlimited bandwidth, we obtain a closed-form capacity proportional to the square root of power. For randomly varying loss, we determine exact finite-energy capacities when the channel realization is publicly revealed, distinguishing knowledge before and after transmission. When fading remains unobserved, we derive capacity bounds and explicit formulas for an on/off channel. We also establish strong-converse bounds, with exact thresholds for the deterministic loss models considered here, observed fading, and unobserved fading with finitely many possible transmissivities. Under mean energy constraints, these thresholds generally exceed the corresponding finite-energy capacities. These results guide energy allocation and provide benchmarks for energy-constrained optical quantum communication with multimode signals and variable loss.
summary: This paper provides exact formulas for the two-way quantum and secret-key capacities when transmitting quantum information through multimode channels suffering from bosonic loss and fading. By employing advanced information-theoretic techniques, the authors establish that these capacities are equal under optimal adaptive protocols. The results are vital for guiding energy allocation in energy-constrained optical quantum communication systems.
main_problem: The paper determines the exact two-way quantum and secret-key capacities for quantum communication over multimode bosonic loss and fading channels.
main_result: The two-way capacities ($Q_2, D_2, P_2, K_2$) are found to be equal and are characterized by specific capacity functions $F_\eta(N)$ or $C_{B,\eta}(P)$ under finite-energy or power constraints.
method: The authors use optimization techniques, including sector teleportation simulation and applying relative-entropy identities, to establish both upper and lower bounds on the achievable rates.
model_or_system: The system involves quantum communication over multimode bosonic channels subjected to general loss ($\eta_j$) and fading. The analysis extends to continuous frequency-dependent loss under a power constraint.
key_observables: Two-way quantum capacity ($Q_2$), entanglement distribution capacity ($D_2$), private classical capacity ($P_2$), and secret-key capacity ($K_2$).
important_parameters: Mean photon-number constraint ($N$), total input power budget ($P$), and channel transmissivities ($\eta_j$).
main_assumptions: The analysis distinguishes between the case where channel fading is publicly revealed versus when it remains unobserved, and it compares finite-energy capacities against strong-converse bounds.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate comparisons between exact capacity calculations and results from different feasible allocations, particularly in multi-mode examples.
paper_structure: The paper systematically derives capacities for finite-mode systems, extends these results to continuous frequency-dependent loss, and analyzes the specific cases of observed and unobserved fading channels using entropy bounds.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, exact capacity formulas for realistic, lossy quantum channels, which is crucial for designing practical quantum communication protocols in optical systems.

FIG. 4. Structure of the proof. The single-mode block estimate (lemma 1) yields the adaptive replica and finite-list bounds (lemmas 3 and 5). Scalar duality and spectral tail estimates turn these into the continuum converse. The sector resource (lemma 2) supplies finite-dimensional hashing, first for discrete modes and then for spectral intervals. Together these branches prove theorem 4. Evaluating the flat-profile integral gives theorem 5. The threshold statements also use the unconstrained resource comparison and public vacuum randomization, as detailed in Appendices E and I.
